messages:
Camille H.: quick follow-up on the heuristic anchoring idea — worried about region safety when anchors use long historical latency. could penalize small regions during warmups and cause capacity thrash. any concerns?
Bryan K.: +1 worried too. anchoring reduces variance but it can entrench a bad initial view. saw this in sim when a new ap-south region had sparse probes.
Alice C.: curious — do we have numbers from the last sim run? iirc anchor_window was 30m there.
Bryan K.: sim summary: new region had 12 samples, mean latency 220ms, anchor pulled it to 310ms after a few outliers. result: routing pushed traffic away and the region never warmed up.
Dinesh R.: hmm. maybe we should separate anchor (historical bias) from probe weight (live signal). treat anchor as a soft prior with TTL and decay.
Jonah M.: love that. concretely: anchor_weight=0.2, probe_weight=0.8, anchor_ttl=5m. gives quick recovery.
Camille H.: idea: make anchor window adaptive by sample count. if samples < N, shrink anchor influence. e.g., anchor_influence = min(0.5, samples/50).
Alice C.: that sounds reasonable. edge-case: spiky regions with high variance might oscillate if anchor influence is tiny. need smoothing.
Bryan K.: agree. maybe two levers: sample-based anchor and variance-penalty smoothing. variance_penalty = sigmoid(stddev - baseline) to nudge towards stable regions.
Dinesh R.: also consider admission: during warmup give a small guaranteed fraction of traffic to new/low-sample regions so they get real load. call it "seed-traffic". tiny amount but enough to collect useful metrics.
Camille H.: seed-traffic is nice. could be tenant-configurable per-region. default 2% for regions with <50 samples.
Jonah M.: operationally, we must ensure this doesn't blow SLAs. seed traffic should be routed to lower-priority models or capacity tiers to limit customer impact.
ops-bot: deploy: canary policy update rolled to staging at 2026-03-20T14:02Z :rocket:
Alice C.: ok putting this into a short proposal: 1) make anchor influence a function of sample count 2) introduce anchor_ttl short by default (5-10m) 3) add seed-traffic fraction for low-sample regions 4) keep variance smoothing to prevent oscillation.
Bryan K.: +1. i'll prototype the sample-based influence in the sim harness. will run a few runs with noisy ap-south and eu-north to check thrash.
Dinesh R.: one more note: policy engine interface needs a small change — expose sample_count and region_variance as inputs to the scorer so adapters can opt-in.
Camille H.: agreed. we should keep backward compatibility: new inputs optional with sensible defaults. add feature flag to enable opt-in behavior for tenants.
Jonah M.: timeline? Bryan, Dinesh, can we have an initial sim report in 3 days? then ops can canary the staging policy.
Bryan K.: aiming for 3 days. will ping here with results.
ops-bot: note: policy-sim-run #546 uploaded to /sim-results/546 at 2026-03-20T16:40Z
Camille H.: thanks everyone. i'll draft the RFC follow-up with config snippets and rollout playbook. posting a short example config below for discussion:
```
policy: 
  anchor: 
    base_weight: 0.2
    ttl: 5m
    sample_threshold: 50
    influence_formula: "min(base_weight, samples / sample_threshold)"
  probe: 
    weight: 0.8
  seed_traffic: 
    enabled: true
    fraction: 0.02
  variance_smoothing: 
    enabled: true
    window: 10m
```
Camille H.: open question: should seed_traffic be tenant-level or global? leaning tenant-level to avoid surprising tenants with forced traffic.
Alice C.: tenant-level makes sense. ops can set global defaults.
Dinesh R.: ok. i'll sketch the scorer PR to accept sample_count/variance inputs. will mark backwards-compatible.
Bryan K.: will run sims and post results. thanks — this feels like a solid path forward. :+1:
